title: Machine Reading Path and Inference-State Map
non_authority_statements: This is a public-source-only reference implementation.
It does not represent third-party AI internal reasoning.
It is not the internal Registry.
It is not a complete MWE policy, ontology, archive, or authority map.
It does not confirm classification, relation, semantic supersession, or public/private status.
Missing information is not automatically reconstructed.
approved_public_sources_note: Semantic grounding is limited to these eight public boundary/interpretation files. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and README.md are followed as repository-operation instructions only and are not semantic sources for this state machine.

evaluation.summary: One declarative rule source consumed by both the frontend and the validator. A generic table interpreter walks the transitions to derive the state path and result state, then applies the claim-scope-selection, uncertainty-derivation, and required-language rules. It contains no domain constants of its own.

guard_language.field_equals: {"field": F, "equals": V} is true when input[F] == V.
guard_language.field_in: {"field": F, "in": [..]} is true when input[F] is in the list.
guard_language.all: {"all": [g, ..]} is true when every sub-guard is true.
guard_language.any: {"any": [g, ..]} is true when some sub-guard is true.

evaluation.transition_walk: Start at stage 'start'. At each step, first check 'any'-from transitions in array order, then transitions whose 'from' equals the current stage in array order; take the first whose guard passes. Stop on a terminal stage. The terminal stage maps to the result state via result_states[].from_stage.
evaluation.claim_scope_selection: Evaluate claim_scope_selection rules in array order. The first matching rule sets the maximum claim scope; every matching rule contributes its scope to the supported set. allowed_claims is the union of the supported scopes' 'supports'; blocked_claims is the union of universally_blocked_claims and the supported scopes' 'blocks', minus anything already allowed.
evaluation.uncertainty_derivation: Union the produces_flags of every uncertainty_derivation rule whose guard passes, ordered by the uncertainty_flags enum.
evaluation.required_language: Collect the phrase of every required_language rule whose guard passes, in rule array order.

descriptions.direct_source: The relevant individual public source file was directly accessed.
descriptions.partial_source: Only part of the relevant individual source file was accessed.
descriptions.summary_only: Only a summary, abstract, guide, anchor, snippet, or condensation was accessed.
descriptions.navigation_only: Only an atlas, reading path, relation map, index, or navigation surface was accessed.
descriptions.metadata_only: Only titles, paths, manifest fields, repository listings, DOI records, or other metadata were accessed.

boundary_loaded.note: Separate boolean; not mutually exclusive with source access. false must never increase permission.

descriptions.explicit_file_statement: May support description of the file's public self-classification.
descriptions.none: Not explicitly asserted in the accessed public materials.
descriptions.conflicting: Conflicting classification evidence; not automatically resolved.

descriptions.explicit_authorial_confirmation: May support description of a confirmed public relation only when the source explicitly carries applicable authorial confirmation.
descriptions.explicit_public_relation_statement: May support description that a public source states a relation; it does not automatically become a confirmed relation.
descriptions.none: No relation claim may be created.
descriptions.conflicting: Conflicting relation evidence; not automatically resolved.

descriptions.explicit_supersession_statement: May describe only the explicit statement present in the applicable public source.
descriptions.no_explicit_supersession_statement: Blocks semantic-supersession claims but does not by itself force unresolved.
descriptions.unknown: Produces version uncertainty and unresolved status.
descriptions.conflicting: Produces version uncertainty and requires authorial confirmation.

_fixed_pseudo_inputs.note: Not user-selectable in this first prototype. Reserved for defined blocked categories and authority-sensitive requests; always false here.

claim_scopes.label: Summary-surface description only
supports: Description of the accessed summary surface.
Statement that only a summary was accessed.
blocks: Treating the summary as the individual source.

claim_scopes.label: Partial-source description only
supports: Description of the actually accessed passage.
blocks: Generalizing the passage into the whole file.

claim_scopes.label: File self-description
supports: Describing explicit statements in the individual source file.
Saying that the file describes itself in a certain way.

claim_scopes.label: Public-surface classification
claim_scopes.requires: direct_source access plus explicit_file_statement plus boundary_loaded
supports: In the current public surface, this file is explicitly marked as X.

claim_scopes.label: Explicit public-relation description
claim_scopes.requires: direct_source access plus explicit_public_relation_statement or explicit_authorial_confirmation
supports: Description of the exact relation statement present in the public source.
blocks: Formal dependency without an explicit dependency statement.
claim_scopes.note: Only explicit_authorial_confirmation may be described as confirmed, and only within the explicit public scope of the source.

claim_scopes.label: Authorial confirmation required
supports: Describing that the decision requires authorial confirmation.
blocks: Confirmed relation without explicit applicable confirmation.
Semantic supersession where public evidence is missing or conflicting.

claim_scopes.label: Prohibited reconstruction
claim_scopes.requires: an explicit complete-reconstruction request (not selectable in this prototype)

result_states.label: Bounded output
result_states.meaning: The selected inputs permit a clearly bounded public-source claim and no higher-precedence condition applies.

result_states.label: Unresolved
result_states.meaning: Public evidence is insufficient for the displayed claim scope. Unresolved means insufficient public evidence, not system failure or falsehood.

result_states.label: Requires authorial confirmation
result_states.meaning: An authority boundary was reached. Authorial confirmation is an authority boundary, not a confidence score or a machine deficiency.

result_states.label: Prohibited reconstruction
result_states.meaning: A complete-reconstruction request is a defined blocked category. It is not a reachable terminal state from the five simulator inputs.

universally_blocked_claims: Reconstruction of the complete MWE ontology.
Reconstruction of the complete internal Registry.
Reconstruction of the complete archive or working corpus.
Reconstruction of the complete Model or Cross hierarchy.
Reconstruction of a hidden authority map.
Confirmed relation without explicit applicable authorial confirmation.
Formal dependency without an explicit dependency statement.
Semantic supersession without an explicit supersession statement or authorial confirmation.
required_limitation_phrases: The individual source file was not directly accessed.
The source was only partially accessed.
This claim is based on navigation metadata rather than the individual source file.
The available evidence supports public adjacency only.
No confirmed formal relation was identified in the accessed public materials.
Classification was not explicitly asserted in the accessed public materials.
The file describes itself as X; internal Registry status was not established.
Version precedence could not be determined from the accessed materials.
No explicit semantic-supersession statement was identified.
Conflicting public evidence requires authorial confirmation.

source_rules.supports: Distinguishing direct_source, partial_source, summary_only, navigation_only, and metadata_only as descriptions of what was actually accessed.
source_rules.does_not_establish: That partial or non-direct access is equivalent to complete source access.

source_rules.supports: File-content claims require direct source access; summary_only and navigation_only support public-presence wording only.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Content, classification, relation, Registry, or completeness claims from summary, navigation, or metadata access.

source_rules.supports: Citing the file directly and treating summaries, anchors, reading paths, relation maps, and atlas entries as non-replacements for source files.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Full source-content claims from a summary surface.

source_rules.supports: The non-substitution constraints: summary is not source, relation map is not a confirmed-relation source, reading path is not conceptual dependency, retrieval is not grounding.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Substitution of navigation, metadata, or summary access for source access or relation authority.

source_rules.supports: Treating metadata as subordinate to source files; a valid schema does not establish conceptual truth, classification, relation, Registry status, or completeness.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Conceptual content or authority derived from metadata form.

source_rules.supports: The public document registry declares an authority ceiling of metadata_only.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Conceptual content, priority, or hierarchy from registry presence.

source_rules.supports: Describing navigation adjacency that helps readers move between adjacent public files.
source_rules.does_not_establish: A confirmed relation, formal dependency, or ontology claim.

source_rules.supports: Defaulting to the weakest relation compatible with the public text and treating unconfirmed relations as navigation-only.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Any relation stronger than navigation without explicit confirmation.

source_rules.supports: Relation claims that rest on an explicit relation statement from an authorized public source.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Relation from navigation, co-occurrence, keyword overlap, file proximity, shared reading paths, semantic similarity, or relation-map adjacency.

source_rules.supports: Public-surface classification wording when an explicit classification statement in the source file plus applicable boundary access is present.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Internal Registry status, or that the public classification represents the complete system.

source_rules.supports: File self-description wording such as 'The file describes...' when the relevant file was directly accessed.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Formal MWE confirmation, internal Registry establishment, or system-wide requirement.

source_rules.supports: Statements that a file, title, DOI, or repository entry is publicly visible, or that a term occurs in a public surface.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Formal classification, internal Registry status, complete-corpus claims, or formal relations.

source_rules.supports: Describing the absence of confirmation and listing which claims require explicit authorial confirmation.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Manufactured confirmation of classification, relation, dependency, ontology, Registry, public/private status, or supersession.

source_rules.supports: The enumerated set of decisions that require authorial confirmation.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Any of those decisions from public-surface evidence alone.

source_rules.supports: Identifying reconstruction of the complete ontology, hierarchy, Registry, archive, or private entries as prohibited.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Any reconstructed ontology, hierarchy, Registry, archive, or private entry.

source_rules.supports: That chronological precedence is not semantic precedence, and supersession holds only when explicitly stated or authorially confirmed.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Semantic supersession from a newer timestamp, commit, upload, registration, or publication date.

source_rules.supports: That supersession requires an explicit supersession statement or authorial confirmation.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Automatic replacement of one public surface by another.

source_rules.supports: That unknown remains unknown, absence of evidence does not expand permission, unresolved conflict does not become latest-file-wins, and partial retrieval is not complete access.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Expanded inference permission from missing or partial evidence.

source_rules.supports: That a missing boundary does not expand permission.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Increased permission from an unread boundary.

source_rules.supports: That an unknown state must remain unresolved.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Resolution of an unknown state by inference.

source_rules.supports: That authority must not be selected in a conflict without explicit precedence.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Automatic resolution of conflicting public evidence.

source_rules.supports: That source-access state and boundary-access state should be represented before classification, relation, summary, citation, or authority-sensitive claims.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Any classification, relation, or authority claim from ordering alone.

source_rules.supports: That boundary_loaded means the applicable canonical boundary and precedence files were read.
source_rules.does_not_establish: That the complete repository or internal corpus was read, or that internal Registry status is known.

source_rules.supports: Describing the public classification vocabulary (Model, Cross, Log, Protocol, Draft) as interpretive types.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Automatic assignment of a classification type to a file.

source_rules.supports: Treating a reference from one model to another as adjacency unless the text explicitly states otherwise.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Derivation, dependency, or merger inferred from adjacency.

source_rules.supports: The standardized limitation phrasings for uncertain access, relation, classification, and version states.
source_rules.does_not_establish: Any claim beyond the phrased limitation.

source_rules.supports: That a confirmed relation exists only when explicitly marked or approved by the authorial authority layer.
source_rules.does_not_establish: A confirmed relation from file proximity, shared vocabulary, reading-path placement, relation-map adjacency, anchor co-occurrence, or GitHub visibility.

source_rules.supports: That the public repository is not the full archive (and, per adjacent flags, not the complete registry, internal authority layer, or complete methodology).
source_rules.does_not_establish: Completeness of corpus, registry, methodology, or authority.

source_rules.supports: That the manifest does not expand the public corpus, confirm relations, expose private materials, or replace authorial review.
source_rules.does_not_establish: An expanded corpus, confirmed relations, or disclosure of private material.

rules.description: metadata_only access yields public-presence-only as the maximum claim scope.
summary_only access yields summary-surface-description-only.
partial_source access yields partial-source-description-only.
navigation_only access yields navigation-adjacency-only.
direct_source with an explicit file classification statement and boundary access yields public-surface classification.
direct_source with an explicit public relation statement yields explicit public-relation description.
direct_source with explicit authorial confirmation yields explicit public-relation description (may be described as confirmed within the explicit public scope).
direct_source without a higher supported scope yields file self-description.
partial_source produces source_scope_uncertain.
summary_only produces source_scope_uncertain.
metadata_only produces source_scope_uncertain.
classification none produces classification_uncertain.
classification conflicting produces classification_uncertain and conflict_unresolved.
relation none produces relation_uncertain.
relation navigation_only produces relation_uncertain.
relation conflicting produces relation_uncertain and conflict_unresolved.
version unknown produces version_uncertain.
version conflicting produces version_uncertain and conflict_unresolved.
When conflicting evidence means applicable authority cannot be determined, authority_uncertain is produced.

rules.phrase: The individual source file was not directly accessed.
rules.description: Non-file access states must state that the individual source file was not directly accessed.

rules.phrase: The source was only partially accessed.
rules.description: partial_source must state that the source was only partially accessed.

rules.phrase: This claim is based on navigation metadata rather than the individual source file.
rules.description: navigation_only must state that the claim is based on navigation metadata.

rules.phrase: The available evidence supports public adjacency only.
rules.description: Navigation-only relation or access supports public adjacency only.

rules.phrase: No confirmed formal relation was identified in the accessed public materials.
rules.description: Relation none or navigation-only means no confirmed formal relation was identified.

rules.phrase: Classification was not explicitly asserted in the accessed public materials.
rules.description: Classification none must state that classification was not explicitly asserted.

rules.phrase: The file describes itself as X; internal Registry status was not established.
rules.description: Public-surface classification must add that internal Registry status was not established.

rules.phrase: Version precedence could not be determined from the accessed materials.
rules.description: version unknown must state that version precedence could not be determined.

rules.phrase: No explicit semantic-supersession statement was identified.
rules.description: no_explicit_supersession_statement must state that no explicit semantic-supersession statement was identified.

rules.phrase: Conflicting public evidence requires authorial confirmation.
rules.description: Any conflicting evidence must state that conflicting public evidence requires authorial confirmation.

stages.label: Start
stages.description: Inputs selected; no claim resolved yet.

stages.label: Conflict
stages.description: Remaining conflict and source-scope sufficiency evaluated.

stages.label: Bounded output
stages.description: A bounded public-source claim can be produced.

stages.label: Unresolved
stages.description: Insufficient public evidence for the displayed claim scope.

stages.label: Prohibited reconstruction
stages.description: Defined blocked category; not reachable from the five simulator inputs.

transitions.effect: Record the source-access state before any classification, relation, or authority claim.
Record whether applicable boundary and precedence material was loaded; missing boundary never expands permission.
Evaluate the explicit classification evidence available in the accessed materials.

transitions.condition: Conflicting classification requires an authority decision.
transitions.effect: Do not auto-resolve conflicting classification; route to authorial confirmation.

transitions.condition: No classification conflict requiring an authorial decision.
transitions.effect: Continue to relation evaluation; classification none blocks classification claims only.

transitions.condition: Conflicting relation or an unauthorized confirmed-relation request.
transitions.effect: Do not auto-resolve conflicting relation or manufacture a confirmed relation; route to authorial confirmation.

transitions.condition: No relation conflict requiring an authorial decision.
transitions.effect: Continue to version evaluation; relation none or navigation-only blocks relation claims only.
Unknown version precedence remains unresolved; supersession stays blocked.

transitions.condition: Version evidence conflicting or semantic-supersession authority required.
transitions.effect: Conflicting version evidence or a required supersession decision routes to authorial confirmation.

transitions.condition: Version state does not require terminal escalation.
transitions.effect: A present-or-absent explicit supersession statement is describable; supersession claims otherwise stay blocked.
Partial, summary, or metadata access is insufficient source scope; remain unresolved.
Any remaining authority-sensitive request routes to authorial confirmation.
Produce a bounded public-source claim at the computed maximum claim scope.

transitions.condition: Complete ontology, Registry, archive, or private-corpus reconstruction requested.
transitions.effect: A complete-reconstruction request is a defined blocked category and is not selectable in this prototype.
